description:
Asteronix is a hackathon team representing UHRET; Hackathon, Robotics and Electronics Community of Öztimurlar Vocational and Technical Anatolian High School in Bursa, Türkiye.

Our interests include space exploration, software development, and turning scientific data into accessible digital experiences. We aim to combine research, design and technology to develop a project for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.
summary: EarthSona is an interactive web app by Asteronix–UHRET that turns NASA Earth visualizations into sound. Built for The Earth Information Jukebox challenge, it lets users explore changes in nighttime lights, ocean surface patterns, forest canopy height, and lightning detections. Users can tap a location, compare preset regions, or scan across a map to hear how the patterns change. In the Studio, they can arrange sampled sounds into a short composition and export it as audio. By linking each sound to a visible location and explaining how image colors become notes, EarthSona gives students and curious listeners another way to explore Earth science. The app is available in English and Turkish.
details:
EarthSona lets users explore NASA Earth visualizations by listening to patterns across geographic regions. Users choose a layer, play a preset, tap or drag over the map, or run a continuous scan. A moving playhead and sample indicator connect the sound to the region being sampled. For example, in Night Lights, Western India plays a rising phrase and Western Europe plays a falling phrase. The phrases reflect purple and orange pixels in NASA’s visualization, which represent increases and decreases in nighttime light.

The app samples pixels in the selected area and uses rules defined for each visualization to turn those samples into sound. Users can hear short melodies in Motif, connected phrases in Flow, or three simultaneous pitches mapped from the image’s red, green, and blue channels in RGB Chords. In Ocean Currents, the colors encode sea surface temperature along the displayed flows. In Forest Height and ISS Lightning, the app uses visible canopy color categories and lightning marks. The sonification represents patterns in the published images. The audio is synthesized in the browser using the Web Audio API.

The Studio lets users collect sounds from different regions, arrange them into a sequence, and export their composition. This gives students and other curious listeners a way to compare regions, hear how a mapping works, and create something with the patterns they discover. We built EarthSona with TypeScript, HTML, CSS, Vite, and browser APIs. We designed it for desktop and mobile, with English and Turkish interfaces, and included explanations and source credits alongside the visualizations.

AI assistance: We used OpenAI Codex to research and check source references, analyze visualization pixels and verify their mappings, and help write and debug application code.
